title: Chapter 280: Door Knocker
html:
No cars passed along the road, and an unnatural silence hung over the area. The occasional stray cat wandered by, only to hurry away as if sensing that something was wrong. “Who are you?”

The investigator stood in the dark, muddy alley. His shoes were gone, leaving his bare feet planted amid heaps of refuse as blood trickled from his wounds.

“Have you forgotten my voice already?” The man slowly emerged from the shadows, a fearsome hammer in his hands. The streetlamps stretched his shadow across the ground. A man had spoken, but the silhouette belonged to a long-haired woman. At last, the investigator saw his face clearly. He gritted his teeth and forced out a name. “Chen Ge!”

“I don’t know you, yet you know my name. It seems my theory was correct.”

The man blocking his escape was none other than Chen Ge. He and Captain Yan had searched the entire third building without finding the final Society member.

By then, Chen Ge already had his suspicions. After obtaining the hospital’s address from Captain Yan, he had returned to New Century Park for his hammer, then hurried to the People’s Hospital to lay an ambush.

“How did you figure it out?” The investigator became unexpectedly calm. A strange smile spread across his face as he stared at Chen Ge.

“Why should I tell you?” Chen Ge switched on the recorder and advanced into the alley, hammer in hand.

“Killing me won’t benefit you. You’re speaking to one of my scapegoats. And in case you’ve forgotten, this body belongs to a police officer.” Though initially shocked to see Chen Ge, the investigator quickly regained his composure. “If I die, this officer dies with me.”

Chen Ge had no time for verbal sparring. The phone in his pocket was recording their conversation. As the hammer drew closer, the investigator’s lips twitched. Chen Ge’s expressionless face seemed to say, Neither of us is a good man, so don’t bother threatening me with cheap tricks.

“We could sit down and have a civilized conversation. Aren’t you curious about my true identity? Don’t you want to know who I am?” The patient tried desperately to engage him, but Chen Ge did not appear interested in talking.

As Chen Ge continued closing the distance, the patient changed tactics. “Don’t you want to know who the chairperson really is?”

“The chairperson’s identity is a multiple-choice question. I’m simply eliminating the wrong answers until only the correct one remains.” It was Chen Ge’s oblique way of saying that the investigator would not survive the night.

Chen Ge had no intention of killing an innocent man. He had acted behind Captain Yan’s back because he intended to capture the investigator and take him to the Haunted House for interrogation. There, after all, Chen Ge would have the numerical advantage.

“I’ll restrain him before turning him over to the police.” He said it for the benefit of the phone still recording in his pocket. His actual plan was to break the investigator’s legs, leaving him alive but unable to escape. The investigator failed to find an opening in Chen Ge’s defenses, yet his expression barely changed. He clearly had another card to play.

“Chen Ge, what I’m about to say will certainly interest you. Let me leave, and I’ll tell you why the doors appear—and how to open and close them.” The investigator wore an inscrutable expression, halfway between a smile and a grimace. He seemed certain that Chen Ge would want what he offered.

“Think carefully. You know how valuable this information is.” Though he spoke calmly, the investigator retreated another two steps. “The officer before you is merely a scapegoat. Only a third of my consciousness occupies this body. Even if you kill him, I’ll remain unharmed.”

“If it won’t harm you, why are you so desperate to escape?” Chen Ge slowed his advance. “Show me your sincerity. That’s the prerequisite for any deal.”

The investigator released a quiet breath of relief. “Since you’re interested in the doors, I assume you know the location of at least one.”

“Indeed,” Chen Ge admitted.

“The circumstances behind a door’s formation are extremely complicated; no one truly understands them. I only know that doors appear where Yin energy gathers and few people venture. Those are merely secondary conditions, however. The crucial factor is the existence of someone who knocks.”

“Someone who knocks on the door?”

“The world behind a door is stained not only red, but with despair and anguish. Every negative human emotion gathers there. Unlike our world, it is filled with endless nightmares.” The investigator lowered his voice. “Ordinary people cannot see it. Only those whose minds have collapsed, or who have lost all hope, have a chance to push open such a door.

“I once heard this from the first person to push one open. That day, he went about his life as usual. He did nothing different. As always, he opened a door he passed through every day—but the world beyond it had completely changed. The door appeared without the slightest warning.”

“Without warning?”

“Yes. You possess a door yourself, so you must have experienced something similar. For instance, you’re standing outside it when suddenly you hear…”

Sirens wailed beyond the alley, cutting him off. Several police cars were speeding toward them!

“Did you call the cops?” The smile on the investigator’s face instantly disappeared.

Chen Ge shook his head. “Continue. Tell me more about the door, and I can help you escape this.”

“Will you?” The investigator laughed coldly.

“You have no other choice.” Chen Ge glanced around for somewhere to hide the hammer.

“I’m a resident of hell. Do you think one demon would trust another?” The investigator spun around and fled down the alley, with Chen Ge close behind.

“Don’t move!” The other end of the alleyway was blocked by another police car. The investigator’s path was blocked. He did not hesitate and ran back into the hospital.

Is he trying to use the complicated layout to escape, or is he trying to find a hostage?

As Chen Ge pursued him, he quickly discovered that he had badly underestimated the investigator’s ruthlessness and resolve.

The madman kicked open a door and raced toward the hospital roof.

“Don’t come any closer!” The investigator stepped on the railing. He was just inches away from the building’s edge!

The night wind whipped at his patient’s gown. The city sprawled beneath his feet as he stood against the darkness, gazing down at everything below.

Chen Ge stopped three meters away, careful not to pressure him further.

“Chen Ge, I’ve remembered your name. Next time we meet, I’ll give you a surprise.” A smile bloomed on the investigator’s face. He looked at Chen Ge and slowly opened his arms.

The rooftop’s safety door was pushed open, and Captain Yan and his men rushed out.

“Yao Qinyi!”

Seeing them, the smile on the investigator’s face turned brighter. He leaned slowly backward like he was returning to the embrace of the dark night.
